screenshots.answer_summary: Computed observations show F-101 differential pressure of 1.38 bar (PT-101 3.62, PT-102 2.24), above the 0.80 bar alarm limit. FT-101 delivery is 52.5 m³/h against a 69.4 m³/h baseline. The reference row has the same timestamp as the current row, so I treat it as a comparison state, not a time trend. Versus that reference, filter dP rose from 0.30 to 1.38 bar, flow fell, and pump head rose from 25.7 to 34.0 m. That is consistent with added resistance in the series path P-101A → J-DISCHARGE → F-101 → V-101 → V-102, with the pump moving up its curve. Tank level is 4 m (66.7%) with no low-level interlock, so tank buffering is not limiting. A downstream restriction would normally raise PT-102, and it fell, so that is less likely. Elevated filter resistance is the leading hypothesis, not proven. A pressure transmitter error or a pump-side difference remain possible. Next experiment: run a server-recomputed changeover to P-101B. If dP stays high at similar flow, the resistance is downstream of the pump. No comparison result has been supplied, so I give no predicted numbers.

evidence.label: Filter differential pressure
evidence.value: 1.38 bar (PT-101 3.62 bar, PT-102 2.24 bar), alarm limit 0.80 bar
evidence.source: current_observations.values.filter_dp_bar / alarm filter-dp (computed simulation, not field measurement)

evidence.label: Pump head and controls
evidence.value: 33.98 m at 100% speed, P-101A active, V-101 100% open

evidence.label: Reference state
evidence.value: dP 0.30 bar, flow 69.4 m³/h, head 25.7 m, same timestamp

hypotheses.cause: Elevated hydraulic resistance within F-101 (fouling-like). The model does not identify the mechanism.
Restriction elsewhere in the series path, such as V-101 or V-102. Less likely because PT-102 fell.
Pump-side difference or pressure transmitter error affecting the apparent dP.

screenshots.answer_summary: Backup recording (Anthropic Claude, not Gemma). CF1 carries a computed 173.1 m³/h (model-only) versus 464.9 m³/h in CF2, with similar DP (0.702 vs 0.693 bar). Source fact: DPIT-713 is shared and cannot identify one vessel (LF-F2). Since DP is nearly equal but flow is about 63% lower, CF1 appears to have higher computed resistance than CF2. That is a model inference, not a measurement. Propagation: filters are upstream of the finite tank, so the computed inflow of 638.0 m³/h versus outflow of 912.6 m³/h drains the tank at -274.6 m³/h (MODEL-INVENTORY-IMBALANCE, a computed warning, not a PLC alarm). The level is 75%, and the controller effort is 85.7%. Alternatives: partial fouling, a partly closed CF1 inlet/outlet valve, or a gauge/proxy discrepancy. Experiment: run the server-recomputed CF1-to-CF3 changeover from identical tank/controller conditions. If CF1's flow deficit follows the vessel offline, the cause is vessel resistance. If it persists, suspect the branch valves or piping. No what-if numbers are available yet.

evidence.value: 0.7033 bar; source alarm 30 psi, normal 10 psi

evidence.label: Tank imbalance
evidence.value: inflow 638.0 vs outflow 912.6 m³/h; net -274.6 m³/h

hypotheses.cause: Higher CF1 filter resistance (fouling or plugging) than CF2
Partly closed CF1 inlet or outlet isolation valve adding branch loss
Pump speed or VFD setting driving the inventory drawdown, with CF1 contributing less to supply

screenshots.answer_summary: Claude backup recording (provider: Anthropic). P-2A is a duty pump, but the computed readings show it passing 218.5 m³/h while P-2B passes 529.4 m³/h, both at 85.7491% speed. Linked speeds are identical, so the flow split is not a speed-setting difference. Source fact: duty pumps are rated 3000 USgpm each (LF-F4). Computed observation: the tank is at 4.572 m (75%) with a +164.7 m³/h inventory imbalance (inflow 912.6 vs outflow 747.9). That is a model-only diagnostic, not a PLC alarm. Tank buffering means upstream filter changes affect inventory before delivery, so filter DP alone does not explain P-2A's low share. Alternatives for the low P-2A flow: higher P-2A branch resistance (partly closed suction, check, or discharge valve), a degraded pump curve, or a model-side asymmetry. Computed pressures cannot separate these. The most informative experiment is the server-recomputed P-2A to P-2C changeover at identical tank and controller conditions. If the low share moves with the pump, P-2A is implicated. If it stays with the branch, valves or piping are more likely. No what-if numbers are available yet.

evidence.label: Tank inventory imbalance
evidence.value: Inflow 912.6 m³/h, outflow 747.9 m³/h, net +164.7 m³/h

evidence.label: Rated pump duty
evidence.value: 3000 USgpm at 35 ft TDH each; any two operate, third is spare

hypotheses.cause: Elevated P-2A branch resistance, such as a partly closed suction isolation, check valve or discharge MOV
P-2A degraded head-flow performance relative to P-2B at the same speed
Leak or asymmetry elsewhere in the shared discharge path, or a VFD setting difference not visible in the linked-speed proxy
